0.description: The whole bottom arc of the drawn tray: at the centre a small figure with its head at the rim and bent arms bringing both fists to the chest around a disc; either side of it a tight spiral with a tail, and beyond those two splayed, cross-hatched creatures seen from above.
0.iconography: The figure is the 'bust holding a disc' copied on KBA_17553, here in place. The tailed spirals read as coiled serpents; the splayed creatures as lizards, frogs or tortoises. The foot of the tray is guarded by coiled and crawling animals.

panel.title: Survey drawing of a large round Ifá tray (48 cm): hooded face, cowrie blocks, gourds and coiled serpents
panel.object_type: pen-and-ink survey drawing of a round opon Ifá
panel.summary: Drawing no. 4, captioned 'Ifabrett 48 cm, Yoruba 3'. At the head a face inside a pointed, hatched hood; either side, blocks of oval seed- or cowrie-like units, then pairs of gourds, zigzag bands and two D-shaped cartouches. At the foot a small figure holding a disc between two coiled serpents and two splayed creatures.

register_readings.reading: Head (undetected): a face in a pointed hood, flanked by blocks of oval cowrie- or kola-like units and pairs of gourds.
Sides (undetected): zigzag bands and a D-shaped cartouche on each side, mirrored.
Foot: a figure holding a disc, between coiled serpents and splayed creatures.

panel.composition: Head–foot axis with near-perfect left–right mirroring: every motif on one side has its twin on the other.
panel.narrative: The richest of the drawn trays. Its head and foot are the two 'faces from an Ifá board' copied separately on KBA_17553, which ties that sheet to this tray. The border reads as the world of the consultation: cowries or kola (payment and offering), medicine gourds (àdó), and at the foot a devotee holding a small round object — perhaps an ikin nut — guarded by coiled serpents. The hooded head shares its pointed frame with the leaders of the Ado-Ekiti door.
panel.hypotheses: Neutral for 'chronicle'. The blocks of oval units are countable and worth checking for 'pattern as number'.
cross_panel_links: Its head and foot figures are copied on KBA_17553.
uncertainties: The single box covers only the foot; the head and sides are undetected.
The ovals could be cowries, kola nuts or leaves.
